articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft patches a staggering 167 vulns including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously named 'BlueHammer' Defender flaw. Meanwhile Chrome hits zero-day #4 because apparently browsers are just swiss cheese now.

articles.title: The Internet Still Works: SmugMug Powers Online Photography
articles.summary: Congress tries to slip another surveillance fig leaf past us with the 'Foreign Intelligence Accountability Act.' Because nothing says accountability like warrantless spying with a prettier name.

articles.title: 20-Year-Old Malware Rewrites History of Cyber Sabotage
articles.summary: Windows RPC gets pwned by 'PhantomRPC' - an architectural weakness with five different exploit paths. Microsoft's spaghetti code strikes again, this time with privilege escalation sprinkles.

articles.title: Parsing Agentic Offensive Security's Existential Threat
articles.summary: Meet 'fast16' - the malware that rewrites cyber sabotage history by predating Stuxnet by five years. Turns out industrial chaos had a prototype nobody knew about.

articles.title: CIA Ran MK-ULTRA Experiments on Prisoners of War in U.S. Custody, Declassified Docs Confirm

articles.title: Kash Patel Got Arrested for Public Urination After a Night of Drinking

articles.title: Checkmarx Confirms GitHub Repository Data Posted on Dark Web After March 23 Attack

articles.title: Litecoin Suffers Denial-of-Service Attack Due To Network Bug — Details

articles.title: GoDaddy Gave a Domain to a Stranger Without Any Documentation
